floor_z_m.method: floor probes with the vertical gripper (calibrate_floor.py, TCP -0.1112 at contact) minus the jaw-tip offset 0.015; homing-tick joint zero
floor_z_m.previous: -0.100: owner's tape measure, base top 100 mm above the floor (Oct 23), in the old model

floor_tcp_z_m.frame: arm base (so101_kinematics), TCP pointing straight down, gripper closed
floor_tcp_z_m.method: calibrate_all.py: touches on the floor (and on the floor board less its 1.25 mm)

wrist_image_jacobian.unit: image fraction (u right, v down) per metre of measured TCP motion (arm base x, y)
wrist_image_jacobian.pose: gripper vertical (homing-tick joint zero), roll 0, TCP at (0.233, 0, -0.017): 0.094 m above the floor TCP height
wrist_image_jacobian.method: wrist_calib.py: +/-0.02 m moves over a brick, llama.cpp 26B box centres, least squares over 6 frames (rms 2.7 px)

previous.note: Oct 23, measured with the old joint zero (gripper ~28 deg off vertical)

wrist_grasp_pixel.unit: wrist image fraction (u right, v down) of the Gemma box centre; height = measured TCP z - floor_tcp_z
wrist_grasp_pixel.meaning: where the block appears when it sits where the jaws will grip it (flush against the fixed jaw, centred on the jaw blades), at each gripper height; TCP pointing straight down, roll 0
wrist_grasp_pixel.method: teach 2026-10-23: owner placed the block between the open jaws; the first close nudged it flush against the fixed jaw (no grip: jaws too high); frames from the closed pose and straight lifts of 3, 6, 10 cm
wrist_grasp_pixel.validity: single teach; the block's long side along robot y (left-right)

front_camera.method: calibrate_front.py: turn test, straight drive at a brick, wrist check at the reach point

wrist_jaws.unit: wrist image fraction (u right, v down)
wrist_jaws.meaning: fixed jaw (right) in the wrist image: its tip row and its inner edge column just below the tip
wrist_jaws.method: median of jaw_geometry over 213 saved plan_wrist/pre_close frames

wrist_descent.unit: depth: metres from the camera to the jaw tips along the descent; p0: wrist image fraction (u right, v down)
wrist_descent.meaning: a floor point's image offset from p0 scales as 1 / (depth_m + h), h = jaw tips above the floor, TCP pointing down
wrist_descent.method: calibrate_descent.py over 49 logged straight descents: depth from box width ratios, p0 least squares on box edges

wrist_grasp_target.unit: wrist image fraction (u right, v down) of the brick's box: its right edge and middle
wrist_grasp_target.meaning: where the brick sits just before closing when held by its middle (owner's teach)
wrist_grasp_target.method: teach_grasp.py: owner placed the red block between the open jaws at the grasp height

gripper_opening.meaning: jaw opening (mm, at the tips) against the gripper angle (deg open from its recorded closed end): straight between these [deg, mm] points; beyond the last, its last segment's slope
gripper_opening.method: calibrate_all.py gripper step: closed at the pick's speed until the stall on nothing and a 2x4 brick (its short and long side, as a pick grasps it); other widths kept from before

points.what: the 2x6 brick across its long side (6 studs)
the 2x6 brick across its long side (6 studs)

cameras.meaning: camera intrinsics (K, dist: OpenCV), the wrist camera's pose in the TCP frame and the front camera's pose in the arm base frame (metres); base_turn_centre: (x, y) the base turns about (m); floor_z: the floor under the floor board the cameras were placed against (its top less floor_board_thickness_m, a ruler's) (m); joint_offsets_deg: the zero offsets the solve assumed (deg, added to the measured angle; empty = none, the arm's own zeros)
cameras.method: solve_cameras.py on capture_cameras.py scenes: calibrateCamera, radial k1 k2 only (the front lens with the base sweep and the side board close-up); Park-Martin hand-eye refined with every corner's reprojection over all scenes, each with its own board poses; the front camera through each scene's wrist board, averaged

joint_stall_thresholds.meaning: per arm joint, the load (fraction of the motor's full scale) above which a (nearly) still joint counts as stalled, proposed for robot_bridge.STALL_LOAD_THRESHOLDS; not applied
joint_stall_thresholds.method: calibrate_all.py: the 99.5 percentile of each joint's load while still over the run (probes and floor touches left out), times 1.5; at least the highest load times 1.2
